title: A Differential Approach to the Generation and Quality Assessment of Synthetic Data for Environmental Monitoring
summary: Asks which generator to choose when an environmental dataset is small, using a 297-sample geochemical table of 25 log-transformed elements, and compares a parametric Gaussian copula against TVAE on marginal fidelity, correlation preservation, privacy and a composite quality score, with a rare-earth subgroup analysis. GAN-based alternatives including CTGAN and CopulaGAN were deliberately excluded on the grounds that they need far more training data than field monitoring provides. The copula wins on global correlation preservation while TVAE better replicates marginals, holds local correlations and is harder to distinguish from real data. Both generators are SDV's, the paper naming the Synthetic Data Vault as the package through which the Gaussian copula is commonly deployed, and every reported score is an SDMetrics metric: KSComplement, CorrelationSimilarity, LogisticDetection and QualityScore. SDV supplies both the generators under test and the measuring instruments.

TVAE, released alongside CTGAN, is one of the three synthesisers it is measured against on t-SNE distribution alignment, fidelity and machine-learning adaptability; CTGAN itself is named in the related-work account of GAN approaches to mixed types and imbalance but is not among the models run.
evidence: the baselines section describes TVAE as a VAE model designed for tabular data using Gumbel-Softmax for categorical and numerical features and retains it for its public availability; Figure 3 compares TVAE against real data on 2D and 3D t-SNE; the results section reports the proposed model outperforming TVAE and CTABGAN on ML adaptability; CTGAN appears only in the related-work paragraph on GAN-based approaches

title: Diffusion Models for Tabular Data Imputation and Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Proposes MTabGen, a diffusion model for mixed-type tabular data that makes three changes to TabDDPM: an encoder-decoder transformer replaces the MLP denoiser, the conditioning features reach the decoder through the attention mechanism as key and value rather than by adding their embedding to the masked features, and the split between conditioned and masked columns is redrawn per row during training, so one model covers both synthetic data generation and missing-value imputation. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generative baselines it is measured against across ten datasets, run from the SDV distribution and tuned under the same Bayesian search budget as the diffusion models.
evidence: section 5.2 lists CTGAN and TVAE among the synthetic data generation baselines and footnote 3 states that the implementation used for both is the one provided at sdv.dev; Table 2 reports their ML efficiency on ten datasets, Table A2 gives their hyperparameter search space, and Table B1 compares their training and sampling cost

title: Efficient mortality prediction for acute respiratory failure: a resource-constrained machine learning approach using MIMIC databases
summary: Builds a mortality predictor for acute respiratory failure that is deliberately cheap to train and deploy, drawing cohorts from MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV and testing whether class rebalancing by synthetic generation improves sensitivity, the metric that matters when a false negative is a missed death. All three generators used are SDV synthesizers run from the library: CTGAN, CopulaGAN and TVAE each produce balanced training sets at fixed class ratios, and the reported sensitivity gains across the classifiers rest on their output.

title: Enforcing Privacy-By-Design: A Policy-Guided Synthetic Data Generator for GenAI Workflows
summary: Proposes a privacy-by-design architecture in which the jurisdiction's rules — GDPR, HIPAA, CPRA — are resolved at generation time rather than bolted on afterwards, with Azure Purview classifying sensitive columns and Apache Atlas enforcing policy over the metadata. SDV is the synthesis engine those policies drive: the contribution is the policy layer, but the data it emits is produced by running the library.
venue: Conference on Cloud and Big Data Computing
evidence: abstract: "The architecture leverages open-source tools, including the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) for synthesis, Azure Purview for the detection of sensitive data, and Apache Atlas for policy enforcement on metadata"

title: Enhancing Semi-Supervised Learning in Educational Data Mining Through Synthetic Data Generation Using Tabular Variational Autoencoder

TVAE is the whole mechanism and TVAE ships in SDV, but the abstract names no implementation, so whether the library was run is unconfirmed.

title: FEST: A Unified Framework for Evaluating Synthetic Tabular Data
summary: Argues that synthetic tabular data is usually judged on a handful of privacy measures such as distance to closest record and nearest neighbour distance ratio, which say little on their own, and assembles FEST, a framework pulling distance-based, attack-based and utility metrics into one evaluation run so the privacy and utility of a generator can be read together. Six generators are implemented and run across the datasets to exercise the framework: CTGAN, Gaussian Copula, CopulaGAN, TVAE, a Gaussian mixture, and a random sampler included as a deliberately leaky control. Four of the six are SDV synthesizers, and the reported tables compare them metric by metric, with distance to closest record highest for CTGAN and nearest neighbour distance ratio highest for CopulaGAN. The SDV family therefore constitutes the bulk of the empirical program the framework is validated on.
evidence: the methods section states that to validate the framework across different data generation techniques the study implements and evaluates Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN), Gaussian Mixture, Gaussian Copula, CopulaGAN, TVAE and a Random Model, generating for each a synthetic dataset the same size as the original; the introduction notes that existing studies rely mainly on limited privacy metrics such as Distance of Closest Record and Nearest Neighbor Distance Ratio, citing Xu et al., 2019 among others; the results state that NNDR was highest for CopulaGAN while DCR was highest for CTGAN, and that the Random model posed the highest attack-based risk; table 3 reports Wasserstein, KS, pairwise and Spearman correlation, mutual information and Jensen-Shannon values for CopulaGAN, CTGAN, Gaussian Copula, the Gaussian mixture, TVAE and the random model

title: Four-Dimensional Aircraft Trajectory Prediction with a Generative Deep Learning and Clustering Approach
summary: Predicts medium- and long-term four-dimensional aircraft trajectories for air traffic management, arguing existing methods fit the trajectory distribution poorly. C-CTGAN pairs K-medoids clustering with CTGAN's conditional generator, a named derivative that conditions on cluster membership rather than on column values alone.
evidence: abstract: proposes C-CTGAN, combining K-medoids clustering with CTGAN

title: GAN_BERT: An Advanced Neural Architecture for Effective Fraud Detection on Imbalanced Datasets
summary: Proposes GAN_BERT, a three-stage pipeline for credit-card fraud detection on a dataset where fraud is a fifth of a percent of rows: CTGAN is trained on the minority class alone to produce synthetic fraud records, a stratified loader mixes real majority, real minority and synthetic rows into balanced batches at configurable ratios, and a FinBERT classifier is fine-tuned on those batches. CTGAN is run unmodified as the generator stage, with the conditional generator and discriminator objectives reproduced from the CTGAN paper, so the named model is a composite built around CTGAN rather than a variant of it; the reported precision and recall gains on the minority class rest on the rows it supplies.
evidence: section 3.1, headed Synthetic Data Generation via Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks, states that the generator learns the conditional distribution p(x|c) of the minority set and cites reference 20, the CTGAN paper, for the adversarial setup; Figure 1 places the CTGAN module ahead of the data loader and Figure 2 shows its embedding layer applying conditional filters; section 3.2 defines the synthetic-to-real batch ratio r_syn; no modification to CTGAN itself is described anywhere in the methodology

title: GenAI-Based Jamming and Spoofing Attacks on UAVs

evidence: abstract: Gaussian Copula-based generation model drives the benchmark construction

title: Generating Synthetic Categorical Data for Causal Modelling of Accessibility Barriers

Gaussian copula and CTGAN are the alternatives the Bayesian network method is compared against.
evidence: abstract: Gaussian copula and CTGAN are the alternatives compared against the authors' Bayesian network method

title: Generating survey databases with Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: Develops Wasserstein GAN variants that carry survey sampling weights through training, so that synthetic records reproduce a weighted survey population rather than the unweighted sample, and evaluates them on the 2019 Belgian Labour Force Survey with 146 variables using Wasserstein distance, FID, SVDD, Cramer-von Mises and KL criteria. CTGAN and CopulaGAN are the two comparison generators the authors did not implement themselves: both are run from the SDV package in Python at default parameters, with the paper pointing readers to the DataCebo GitHub of the Synthetic Data Vault project for the code, and noting that CopulaGAN transforms the data before applying CTGAN and that neither incorporates sampling weights. SDV's generators are therefore executed as the external baselines the weighted models are measured against.

title: Improving the Generation and Evaluation of Synthetic Data for Downstream Medical Causal Inference
summary: Argues that synthetic medical data judged only on marginal fidelity can still mislead a downstream causal analysis, and proposes STEAM, which structures generation around a causal graph so that each variable is generated conditional on its parents, together with evaluation targets aimed at causal rather than distributional faithfulness. CTGAN is both a compared generic generator and a substrate STEAM is applied to: the results tables carry a CTGAN row and a STEAM CTGAN row side by side across the datasets, with the STEAM version reported as improving precision and treatment-effect error.
evidence: the taxonomy table places CTGAN and TVAE (both reference 97) among the generic generative models whose distributional target is the joint marginal, against the causal generative models and the paper's own STEAM; the experiments state the authors compare generic tabular data generators with their STEAM counterparts across all three datasets, choosing baselines across the major families, CTGAN, TVAE, ARF, NFlow and TabDDPM; the results tables report CTGAN at 0.889 precision and 0.586 PEHE error on ACTG against STEAM CTGAN at 0.892 and 0.436, with the takeaway that in the vast majority of cases generation via STEAM leads to better performance; reference 97 is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni
needs: STEAM is a model-agnostic wrapper applied over five interchangeable generators, yielding STEAM CTGAN among STEAM TVAE, STEAM ARF and the rest — the same shape as paper-constrained-dgm-realistic-2024 (shard 60), which was recorded derivative_work 4. Recorded api_user 4 here instead, on the reading that STEAM structures generation AROUND a frozen CTGAN rather than entering its losses, which is the GAN_BERT composition test. The two entries should be ruled together, and this is the third model-agnostic-wrapper case after shard 60 and paper-rule-guided-tabular-low-data-2025 in shard 71

title: Is Synthetic Flow Data from Generative Models Ready for Network Intrusion Detection Systems?
summary: Builds one evaluation pipeline for synthetic network-flow data and puts a representative of each generative family through it — a GAN, a diffusion model and a language model — measuring not only distributional similarity but the downstream intrusion-detection performance that follows from training on the generated flows, with attention to minority attack classes. CTGAN is the GAN-family representative: it gets its own methodology subsection describing the conditional generator and training strategy that address mode collapse and imbalanced categoricals, its training and sampling workflow is diagrammed, and it is trained and sampled on the benchmark flows.
evidence: section I states the unified evaluation pipeline assesses three generative models, CTGAN from the GAN family, TabDDPM from the diffusion family and GReaT from the LLM family; section III.B, Overview of CTGAN, describes its two components and Figure 2 illustrates the workflow for training CTGAN and generating synthetic data; section II notes prior studies used CTGAN to generate minority-class instances for NIDS datasets without addressing generated-data quality

title: Joint Relational Database Generation via Graph-Conditional Diffusion Models
summary: Generates a whole relational database jointly rather than table by table, factorizing the distribution into a graph over primary and foreign keys and a graph-conditional diffusion model over the attributes, so that multi-hop inter-table dependencies survive instead of being cut by the conditional-independence assumptions earlier methods rely on. SDV sits on both sides of the evaluation: it is the statistical relational baseline, described as Gaussian-copula-based RDB synthesis, and the fidelity metrics including cardinality are computed with the SDMetrics package.
evidence: the baselines paragraph states the authors compare their model to four relational database generation methods from the literature and that SDV, reference 13, is a statistical method tailored for RDB synthesis based on Gaussian Copulas, set alongside ClavaDDPM and others; the evaluation-metrics paragraph states that to evaluate synthetic data fidelity the authors follow prior work and report metrics implemented in the SDMetrics package, reference 42, beginning with Cardinality, which compares the distribution of the number of child rows per parent row between real and synthetic data, computed for each parent-child pair and averaged; the related-work discussion notes that prior methods resorted to Markov-like conditional independence assumptions of tables or rows given their parents, which is the position SDV's relational approach occupies. Running SDMetrics as the evaluation harness outranks the comparison role, on the DP-CGANS and SDGym precedent

title: Just-in-Time Logic Enforcement
summary: Argues that domain rules should constrain a language model while it generates rather than during training or after inference, and demonstrates LeJIT, which interleaves an SMT solver into token-by-token decoding: before each token the solver instantiates the active rules with the values produced so far, computes the feasible range for the current variable, and prunes tokens from which no compliant completion exists, with a character-level transition system bridging the model's tokens and the solver's variables. A generic GPT-2 guided this way reaches parity with task-specific systems on network telemetry imputation and on synthetic trace generation while satisfying every extracted rule. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generators it is measured against on the generation task.
evidence: section 4.2 lists CTGAN and TVAE, both reference 53, among the synthetic network data generators compared against; Figure 5 reports their Jensen-Shannon divergence against the original distribution for six measurement fields alongside NetShare, E-WGAN-GP and REaLTabFormer

title: On the Gap Between Diffusion and Transformer Multi-Tabular Generation
summary: Asks why a transformer relational synthesiser trails a diffusion one on multi-table data when the two are close on single tables, and attributes the difference to how each represents contextual information and the parent-child link. Two changes close much of the gap: tying the transformer block weights of the parent model to the relational adapter's decoder so only the child vocabulary is fine-tuned, and inserting a cluster identifier as an in-context categorical cue in both tables, an autoregressive stand-in for classifier guidance. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the single-table baselines it benchmarks, and CTGAN is described as the GAN adaptation that handles heterogeneous columns and class imbalance.

title: Improved Techniques for Training Tabular GANs Using Cramer's V Statistics
summary: Starts from a known weakness of CTGAN, that it does not preserve dependencies between categorical columns, and asks whether making that dependency structure explicit during training fixes it. The modification is made inside CTGAN's own loss and critic rather than around a frozen model, and CTGAN is both the substrate and the comparison, so this is a derivative of CTGAN even though the resulting model is never given a name of its own.

TGAN is the generative option set against SMOTE, MWMOTE and ADASYN, so the first-party tabular GAN is benchmarked against three classical oversamplers on insurance claims.

title: Conditional Tabular GAN-Based Two-Stage Data Generation Scheme for Short-Term Load Forecasting
summary: Short-term load forecasting is limited by how little external feature data utilities hold, so this proposes a two-stage scheme that generates the missing features before forecasting. CTGAN is trained on the input variables and sampled to produce them, and is the generation model the scheme is built on.
evidence: section 'A. Data Generation Model: CTGAN' plus the algorithm steps 'Train CTGAN using' and 'Generate using the trained CTGAN'

title: Ensemble-based Synthetic Data Synthesis for Federated QoE Modeling
summary: Addresses the problem that quality-of-experience models need labelled data pooled across subjects while data-protection regulation blocks sharing the local datasets, and proposes synthesising shareable substitutes with an ensemble of Bayesian network models trained at each site. CTGAN is the tabular-GAN prior art the design departs from: the paper credits it with addressing multi-modality and varying distribution in continuous attributes through conditional GANs and preprocessing, then declines to adopt it, judging the per-dataset manual work and the tuning burden across its component algorithms too heavy for the QoE datasets in hand.
evidence: the related-work discussion states that challenges including multi-modality and varying distribution in continuous attributes are addressed with indicative results using conditional GANs and preprocessing techniques, and that these are hard to replicate on the paper's datasets because of the extra manual work per dataset and the complexity of tuning the plurality of algorithms involved; the paper favours a Bayesian ensemble instead. Xplore reports the reference list as unavailable for this document, so the citation is identified from the prose description of CTGAN's two contributions rather than from the bibliography entry

title: Generative Adversarial Networks in Actuarial Modeling- Enhancing Predictions of Long-Tail Risks Done
summary: Argues that long-tail insurance risks are hard to price because the historical record contains too few severe events, and surveys how adversarial generation could synthesize rare-event representations to fill that gap, with a Wasserstein-style stabilization for the training dynamics. CTGAN is cited twice as the reference point for tabular adversarial generation and nothing more: the paper credits Xu et al. with preserving statistical attributes of tabular data while noting they did not address rare events, and misnames the model TabGAN in doing so.
evidence: the introduction states that GANs have demonstrated exceptional capability in generating synthetic data retaining the statistical characteristics of training datasets across multiple domains, citing Xu et al. 2019 as reference 7, and argues this makes them suited to synthesizing rare events; the related-work section states that while GANs have been widely used in image synthesis their application to tabular data remains relatively underexplored, and that Xu et al. (2019) introduced TabGAN for generating synthetic tabular datasets, showing the method preserved key statistical attributes but did not specifically address the challenge of modeling rare events; reference 7 resolves to Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni, Modeling tabular data using conditional GAN. The name TabGAN is the paper's own error for CTGAN, and no CTGAN implementation is run or benchmarked anywhere in the paper

title: Learning Vine Copula Models For Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Casts vine copula structure selection as a reinforcement learning problem, learning tree structures that capture hierarchical dependence in tabular data better than greedy heuristics.
evidence: first-party: this artifact is SDV, not something that integrates it

title: Modeling Tabular Data using Conditional GAN
summary: Introduces CTGAN and TVAE, together with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling to handle imbalanced categorical columns and multi-modal continuous columns. The most cited artifact in the ecosystem and the standard baseline for tabular synthesis.
evidence: first-party: this artifact is SDV, not something that integrates it

title: The Synthetic Data Vault
summary: The founding SDV paper. Introduces generative modeling of an entire multi-table relational database via recursive conditional parameter aggregation, and evaluates it by having data scientists solve predictive tasks on synthetic versus real data with no statistically significant difference in outcome.
evidence: first-party: this artifact is SDV, not something that integrates it

title: Copula Graphical Models for Wind Resource Estimation
summary: Pre-SDV copula work: estimates wind speed at candidate turbine sites from correlated reference sites using copula graphical models. The copula machinery here is the ancestor of the Copulas library and GaussianCopulaSynthesizer.

title: A Systematic Framework for Tabular Data Disentanglement
summary: Sets out a formal framework for tabular data disentanglement, defining the extraction and extrapolation queries a data owner issues, the external knowledge available, and the utility and privacy objectives against which a latent representation is scored, so that otherwise unrelated approaches can be read as instances of one flow. CTGAN and TVAE are named as two of the existing approaches the framework subsumes, cited for conditional generation under specified conditions and for latent-representation learning respectively, with mode collapse and generation quality given as their limitations; neither is run.
evidence: the abstract names factor analysis, CT-GAN and VAE as the existing tabular disentanglement methods whose scalability, mode collapse and extrapolation limitations motivate the framework; section 1 repeats CT-GAN [32] as conditionally generating synthetic data under specified conditions with limitations in efficiency and overall quality, and argues that factor analysis, CT-GAN and VAE can be seen as parts of one general disentanglement flow; a later section groups TVAE [32] with Tabsyn, Switchtab and VAEGMM as following the generic latent-representation approach. Reference [32] is Xu et al. The paper is formal throughout and reports no experiments

title: Active Tabular Augmentation via Policy-Guided Diffusion Inpainting
summary: Argues that distributional fidelity is the wrong objective for augmentation under data scarcity and instead selects what to synthesise by a policy that targets where the current learner is weakest, inpainting the chosen regions with a diffusion model over rounds, and reports gains over augmenters that optimise fidelity alone. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the seven compared augmentation methods, run from their official implementations at the same synthetic budget and data splits as the rest.
evidence: the baselines paragraph lists seven augmentation methods and names the VAE-based TVAE (Xu et al., 2019) and the GAN-based CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) among them, alongside SMOTE, ARF, SPADA, TabDDPM and TabDiff; appendix D.3 states that official implementations with recommended defaults are used and that all methods share the same synthetic budget of 500 samples and the same splits; Tables 9 and 10 and the main accuracy table report CTGAN and TVAE columns at every scarcity level, with related work crediting them as the early methods that transform mixed-type features into a continuous space

title: AdaPCLA: Adaptive Prior-Calibrated Logit Adjustment for Long-Tailed Longitudinal EHR Generation
summary: Addresses the tendency of autoregressive longitudinal electronic health record generators to underrepresent rare diagnosis codes and their co-occurrence structure, by adding a frequency-derived prior bias to the output logits as a temporary training scaffold that is annealed to zero, so the model internalizes rare-event dependencies in its own parameters instead of depending on an external correction at inference, and supports zero-shot adaptation to a population with different code frequencies through a delta-bias correction. CTGAN is present only as a bracket citation in the related work, standing in for the GAN-based tabular generators the longitudinal EHR line has moved past and, in one place, for the conditional tabular generators whose attribute conditioning the paper's zero-shot distribution control is positioned against.

title: Bayesian Generative Adversarial Networks via Gaussian Approximation for Tabular Data Synthesis
summary: Places a Bayesian posterior over a tabular GAN's generator weights without the memory cost of the Markov chain approach, by collecting a running mean and low-rank plus diagonal covariance of the generator weights during training with Stochastic Weight Averaging-Gaussian and sampling from that Gaussian at synthesis time, and reports on five national census tables plus Adult and a churn dataset that the result sits higher on the utility axis of a risk-utility map without a matching rise in attribute-disclosure risk. The model is a named CTGAN variant: SWAG is integrated into CTGAN's own generator, the paper's ablations run averaging-only and several covariance ranks against unmodified CTGAN and a Markov-chain BayesCTGAN, and the implementation is published as a CTGAN fork.
evidence: the abstract introduces Gaussian Approximation of CTGAN (GACTGAN) as an integration of SWAG within the CTGAN generator and states it yields better synthetic data compared to CTGAN; the introduction credits CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) with addressing heterogeneous tabular features by modelling conditional distributions and using training-by-sampling; the contributions list names GACTGAN as putting a Bayesian posterior over the generator and section 4.2.2 defines the variants, including an averaging-only ACTGAN and diagonal and low-rank covariance settings; the complexity discussion compares the training cost directly against the baseline CTGAN complexity; Figures 2, 4, 6 and 7 report CTGAN, BayesCTGAN, ACTGAN and four GACTGAN configurations side by side under Wasserstein and vanilla losses on the UK, Indonesia, Canada, Fiji and Rwanda census tables plus Adult and Churn; the data and code availability statement gives github.com/rulnasution/ctgan-bayes. The variant name appears in the title and abstract, unlike the majority of derivatives found in this project.

title: Can synthetic data overcome the privacy and fidelity bottleneck in Pharmacometrics?
summary: Benchmarks synthetic generation against a daptomycin population pharmacokinetic model, asking whether synthetic patients preserve the structure a compartmental model depends on rather than only the marginals. Gaussian Copula, TVAE and CTGAN are three of five algorithms, each run to produce a hundred synthetic datasets, which is a more rigorous replication design than most of this literature.

title: Cascaded Flow Matching for Heterogeneous Tabular Data with Mixed-Type Features
summary: Targets features that mix a discrete state with an otherwise continuous distribution, such as inflated zeros or missing codes, by generating a coarse categorical sketch of the row first and then conditioning a high-resolution flow-matching model on it through a guided probability path and data-dependent coupling, with a proof that the cascade tightens the transport-cost bound. SDV supplies both sides of the evaluation: CTGAN version 0.11.0 from the sdv-dev repository and TVAE are run as baselines, and the Shape and Trend scores that carry the fidelity results come from SDMetrics version 0.22.0.

title: CausalWrap: Model-Agnostic Causal Constraint Wrappers for Tabular Synthetic Data
summary: Observes that generators trained to match an observational joint distribution can score well on column-wise utility while distorting causal effect estimates, and fits a post-hoc correction module that pulls a trained generator's samples toward a partially known causal structure, evaluated on synthetic structural causal models of three kinds and on a MIMIC-IV intensive-care cohort against an oracle sampler. Two of the three wrapped base generators are SDV, CTGAN and TVAE, each trained in its standard implementation before the wrapper is fitted.
evidence: the experimental setup states that three base generators spanning the GAN, diffusion and VAE families are wrapped, CTGAN [Xu et al., 2019], TabDDPM and TVAE [Xu et al., 2019], each trained using its standard implementation with CausalWrap then fitted as a post-hoc correction module on top; the results table reports per-generator causal error and the change under the wrapper for CTGAN and TVAE across linear-Gaussian, non-linear additive and mixed-type structural causal models against an oracle sampler. The related-work section separately places Causal-TGAN as injecting a known causal graph into CTGAN's conditional generation, which is a distinct approach from the post-hoc wrapper proposed here

title: Data Augmentation via Causal-Residual Bootstrapping
summary: Augments a small tabular dataset by resampling residuals along a known or estimated causal graph, so that added points respect the causal structure rather than only the observed joint distribution, and reports lower downstream error than both a no-augmentation baseline and generative augmenters, several of which prove worse than not augmenting at all. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generative augmentation baselines run at 100 training samples across the reported error tables.
evidence: the experimental section compares causal-residual bootstrapping against SMOTE-style and generative augmenters, listing CTGAN as the GAN-based approach for tabular data and TVAE (Xu et al., 2019) as the variational autoencoder adapted for tables, alongside TabDDPM, ARF and NFLOW, and states the non-causal augmenters are included to check that gains come from causal structure rather than extra points; Figure 4 and the per-variable and per-dataset error tables report CTGAN and TVAE rows throughout, with both recorded as performing worse than no augmentation in the known-graph setting. The paper miscites CTGAN to Bowles et al. (2018) while citing TVAE correctly to Xu et al. (2019)

title: Forensic-Oriented Intrusion Detection Using Synthetic Network Traffic Data and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
summary: Designs an intrusion-detection workflow to forensic standards: the original capture is an immutable, hash-verified artefact that the model is never allowed to touch, and detection runs on XGBoost with SHAP TreeExplainer supplying instance-level attribution. Everything the classifier sees is a synthetic derivative generated by SDV's CTGAN, which puts the library on the chain-of-custody boundary — remove it and the design has no training data it permits itself to use.
evidence: abstract: "Original datasets are treated as immutable, hash-verified artefacts; all training operates on parameterized synthetic derivatives via SDV + CTGAN"

title: Generating High-quality Privacy-preserving Synthetic Data
summary: Proposes a post-processing pipeline that can be slotted after any tabular generator, patching the categorical modes a generator collapses and then filtering samples that sit too close to a training record, and evaluates the trade-off it produces on a joint fidelity, utility and privacy protocol across three benchmarks. The pipeline is built and measured entirely on CTGAN and TVAE, tuned per dataset by Bayesian search, with the SDV implementation of the correct attribution probability supplying the privacy score.
evidence: the evaluation design states that for each of Credit Default, Adult and Cardio the authors train CTGAN and TVAE and then apply mode-patching and the epsilon-ANY filter as post-processing, the stated goal being not a new generator but a pipeline that can be slotted after CTGAN, TVAE or future models; the privacy section states that the SDV implementation returns the correct attribution probability protection score, which is reported as a percentage and summarised by median across attributes; Table II lists the tuned CTGAN generator and discriminator learning rates, embedding and hidden dimensions per dataset, and SDGym is cited as the early fidelity and utility benchmark that neglected privacy

title: Generating Logically Consistent Synthetic Supply Chain Data with LLM-Driven Knowledge Graph Reasoning
summary: Argues that synthetic supply chain records must preserve the operational logic governing them - temporal orderings, arithmetic dependencies, hierarchical taxonomies and conditional rules - and not only their marginal distributions, and builds a framework that first extracts a column relationship knowledge graph using a multi-LLM ensemble with majority voting and then conditions generation on that graph, so that generated records satisfy the discovered constraints rather than merely resembling real ones statistically. CTGAN is one of four compared generators, included as the widely adopted GAN-based framework for tabular synthesis alongside TabDDPM, TabSyn and GReaT.
affiliations: University of Cambridge; Alan Turing Institute
evidence: section 2.1 names existing deep generative models for tabular data including GAN-based approaches such as CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) and argues they are optimized to preserve marginals, correlations and downstream predictive utility rather than operational logic; section 2.2 places CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) and CTAB-GAN+ as the GAN-based direction in the evolution of deep tabular methods; section 4.2 states that the framework is compared against four representative state-of-the-art tabular generative baselines and that CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is included as a widely adopted GAN-based framework for tabular data synthesis, with TabDDPM, TabSyn and GReaT the other three. Importance 3: a compared generator among four, with none of CTGAN's machinery adopted. Same Cambridge group as paper-inter-column-logic-eval-2025 and a direct continuation of it - that paper proposed the inter-column logic metrics, this one builds a generator to satisfy them - so the two are best reviewed together.

title: Generative AI-Based Monte Carlo Simulation for Method Evaluation Using Synthetic Multilevel Data
summary: Sets out a framework for running Monte Carlo simulation studies on AI-generated data that has a multilevel structure, such as students nested in schools, and evaluates how well predictive performance and parameter recovery estimated on synthetic data track the real thing, adding fidelity criteria for within-table, between-table and machine learning utility. CTGAN is one of the two generators the framework is built on, trained on a joined single table after individual-level variables are split into cluster-mean and cluster-demeaned components, then corrected by a new cluster-level consistency alignment step that forces school-level variables to agree within a synthetic school without collapsing their marginals.
evidence: Section 3.3 states the paper trains ClavaDDPM with multiple-table data and CTGAN with join-as-one data and then enhances each with targeted modifications for multilevel generation; section 3.3.2, CTGAN with Cluster-Level Consistency Alignments, restates CTGAN's WGAN-GP minimax objective and refers to Xu et al. 2019 for mode-specific normalization, one-hot encoding and training-by-sampling, then states that because CTGAN is designed for single-table generation it does not preserve hierarchical structure and may assign different school-level values to students in the same school, and introduces cluster-level consistency alignment as a post-processing procedure that enforces identical school-level values while preserving fidelity; section 3.2 states individual-level variables are transformed into cluster-demeaned and cluster-mean components before training; the modifications wrap CTGAN rather than alter its architecture or losses. The bibliography lists DataCebo's Synthetic Data Metrics version 0.12.0 and the text cites SDV as an open-source benchmark for similarity score thresholds

title: Generative Synthetic Data for Causal Inference: Pitfalls, Remedies, and Opportunities
summary: Shows that a tabular synthesizer can pass distributional, privacy and train-on-synthetic-test-on-real checks while still distorting the average treatment effect, because prediction loss penalizes treatment-effect error only through an overlap-weighted term, so a generator can reproduce dominant observed outcomes while underlearning the intervention-relevant contrast; it formalizes the mismatch with sensitivity and loss-decomposition results and proposes a hybrid alternative that generates covariates with a generative model but fits the treatment and outcome mechanisms separately, then uses the result as a pre-analysis simulation engine for comparing OR, IPW, AIPW and TMLE estimators. CTGAN is one of the two generators the whole empirical program runs on, supplying both the fully generative arm and the covariate generator inside the proposed hybrid, and is credited in the related work for introducing conditional GANs with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling.
evidence: the related-work section states that for tabular data CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) introduced conditional GANs with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling; section 3 names GAN-based approaches citing Xu et al. 2019 as one of the two families whose causal fidelity is in question; the ACTG application constructs four synthetic datasets named LLM Full, LLM Hybrid, CTGAN Full and CTGAN Hybrid, and the results table reports each on train-on-synthetic-test-on-real RMSE for the cd420 outcome, mean distance to the closest record, and IPW, AIPW and TMLE treatment-effect estimates; the abstract states that LLM-based hybrid synthesis is often more faithful than CTGAN where causal fidelity can be assessed. Importance 4 on the GAN_BERT precedent: CTGAN runs unmodified as the covariate generator inside the paper's own proposed hybrid framework, not only as a comparison arm, so half the empirical results are CTGAN output and the work does not stand without it. The results table is Table 3, reported over repeated subsamples of 1000, in which CTGAN's cd420 RMSE falls from 244.46 to 107.95 under hybridization. Curated independently by slice A (this record) and slice C (shard 80, paper-generative-synthetic-causal-inference-2026); both reached api_user importance 4 without coordination, and the slice C record has been removed as a duplicate.

title: Interactive 3D visualization of surface roughness predictions in additive manufacturing: A data-driven framework
summary: Builds a predictor for arithmetic mean roughness in material-extrusion additive manufacturing from process parameters and local surface angle, trained on an 87-run Box-Behnken design, and wraps it in a web tool that renders predicted roughness over an uploaded 3D model so the effect of the staircase effect can be seen before printing. Conditional synthetic augmentation is added with a CGAN the authors build themselves; CTGAN is cited as the tabular conditional-GAN methodology their conditional generation follows, but it is not named in prose and not run.
evidence: the related-work section states that for tabular data, conditional GAN variants have been developed to better capture mixed discrete and continuous variables and complex distributions, citing [13], which is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni (2019); section 3.3 describes the augmenter as a CGAN whose conditioning vector holds the scaled process parameters and the surface-inclination descriptor while the generator emits a roughness value, and states the approach is consistent with tabular CGAN methodologies developed for mixed and multimodal numerical data where conditional generation preserves feature dependencies rather than generating unconditional samples, citing [13] again. The generator is the authors' own; no CTGAN row appears in any results table; CTGAN is never named as such in prose, entering only as reference [13]. Curated independently by slice C (this record) and slice D (shard 86, paper-am-surface-roughness-viz-2026); both reached citation_only importance 2 without coordination, and the slice D record has been removed as a duplicate.

title: Machine Learning for Network Attacks Classification and Statistical Evaluation of Adversarial Learning Methodologies for Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Two tasks in one paper: classify network attacks with stable supervised models, then generate synthetic traffic with a spread of adversarial architectures — Vanilla-GAN, WGAN, WGAN-GP, KLD-GAN, CTGAN-2, a diffusion forest and an LLM — and ask which of them is worth keeping. The generators are the authors' own; the judgement is SDV's. Quality Report and Diagnostic Report percentages are averaged into an "SDV Overall Scores" table and a 95% threshold on those scores decides which models advance, so SDV is run as the evaluation harness the whole second half rests on.

title: Measuring the Dependency Gap: Diagnosing Inter-Column Fidelity in Tabular Generative Models
summary: Shows that a fully factorized table, with every column shuffled independently so that all inter-column dependency is destroyed, still passes the commonly reported linear classifier two-sample test on four benchmarks, and replaces it with a gradient-boosted test whose score decomposes into marginal, dependency and numerical-categorical cross terms read against zero-dependency and oracle references. The metrics shown to be blind are SDMetrics': the logistic detection score and the pairwise Trend similarity are computed and reported throughout as the foil against which the new diagnostic is set.
evidence: the related-work section states that the dominant fidelity metrics are the column-wise and pairwise Shape and Trend similarities together with a detection score, as packaged by widely used libraries such as SDMetrics (Patki et al., 2016), whose detection metric trains a logistic-regression discriminator; section 3 reports the linear C2ST as the SDMetrics logistic-detection score and Trend as the SDMetrics pairwise column-correlation similarity, both carried through the results only to demonstrate their blindness, the fully factorized reference scoring 0.995 to 1.000 on the linear test and 0.69 to 0.78 on Trend; section 5 attributes a Trend discrepancy on one dataset to a plausible data-split or SDMetrics-version difference, which establishes that the library itself was run. CTGAN appears only as one citation in a list of GAN-based generators and is not evaluated

title: MobEvolve: An Agentic Self-Evolving Heuristic System for Interpretable Human Mobility Generation

Four SDV single-table synthesizers stand in for the deep tabular generative arm of the comparison, Gaussian Copula, TVAE, Copula-GAN and CTGAN, run from the SDV library and reported on individual, distribution and behaviour metrics as well as generation latency.

title: PluRel: Synthetic Data unlocks Scaling Laws for Relational Foundation Models
summary: Synthesizes whole multi-table relational databases from scratch rather than imitating an existing one, modelling schemas as directed graphs, primary-foreign key connectivity as bipartite graphs and per-table feature distributions through conditional causal mechanisms, and uses the resulting unlimited supply of databases to show that relational foundation model pretraining loss follows power-law scaling in both the number of synthetic databases and total tokens, with the gains transferring zero-shot to real benchmarks. The Synthetic Data Vault is the named prior art the framework departs from: it is cited for the premise that relational databases are rarely public because they hold sensitive information, and again as the privacy-preserving relational generator that reproduces the structure and statistics of a given real database but cannot produce novel ones from scratch.
evidence: the introduction states that relational databases are rarely public because they typically contain sensitive user or enterprise information, citing Patki et al. 2016; the related-work section names privacy-preserving synthetic database generation, citing Patki et al. 2016, as a line of research focused on reproducing the structure and statistical properties of a given real-world database while protecting data subjects; the method motivation states that alternative approaches such as the Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al. 2016), GAN-based and diffusion models can capture characteristics of real-world databases but cannot generate novel ones from scratch without relying on existing real-world examples, which is the limitation the framework is introduced to address. The tight scan returns one hit in the whole PDF and it resolves to the SDV anchor paper, not to CTGAN; nothing SDV-family is run. Importance 2 rather than 1 under the convention for prior art a paper departs from: SDV is named individually in three places with a stated limitation, not listed undifferentiated.

title: Quantifying Membership Disclosure Risk for Tabular Synthetic Data Using Kernel Density Estimators
summary: Proposes a membership inference framework for tabular synthetic data that fits kernel density estimators to member and non-member distance distributions, recovering the probabilistic output and ROC analysis of shadow-model attacks without retraining any generator, and shows through ROC analysis that datasets judged safe on average accuracy can still leak badly at low false positive rates. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the six generators whose output the attack is run against across four datasets, both trained on the real data through the SynthCity framework.
affiliations: Sorbonne University; Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi

title: ReTabSyn: Realistic Tabular Data Synthesis via Reinforcement Learning

SDV appears on both sides of the evaluation: TVAE is run from the official SDV library implementation at its default settings as one of six baselines, and the Shape and Corr. columns of the fidelity table are SDMetrics measures, with marginal similarity aggregated from Kolmogorov-Smirnov and total-variation scores and pairwise correlation similarity computed with contingency similarity for categorical pairs and a mixed-type method, cited to DataCebo's Synthetic Data Metrics.

title: SGN: A Similarity-based Generative Network for Data Generation under Distribution Shift
summary: Trains a generator on a source domain to produce samples aligned with a shifted target domain by learning a shared linear space and a transmission between the two, so that a handful of target samples is enough to augment the target domain usefully, demonstrated on both image and tabular benchmarks. CTGAN and TVAE are the two tabular baselines, implemented from the SDV library with the default structures it states, and the paper attributes their weaker downstream regression and classification results to their being fitted to the source distribution alone.

title: SYNTHONY: A Stress-Aware, Intent-Conditioned Agent for Deep Tabular Generative Models Selection
summary: Treats the choice of tabular synthesizer as the problem worth automating rather than the supply of synthesizers, profiling a dataset along four interpretable stress dimensions - long-tailed marginals, high-cardinality categoricals, Zipfian imbalance and small-sample size - and matching that profile against a capability registry to pick a generator that minimizes regret against an intent-specific oracle, given a user preference over fidelity, privacy and utility. SDV is both prior art and pool: it is named twice as the open-source library that democratized access to individual synthesizers and provides unified APIs and benchmarking but leaves model selection to the user, which is the gap the selection layer fills, it is credited for Gaussian Copulas in the statistical lineage, and TVAE is one of the ten candidate synthesizers the framework selects among.

Importance 3: TVAE is one of ten generators in the selection pool and SDV is described rather than run.

title: SecretFan: Synthesizing Realistic Data without Breaking Privacy

CTGAN is the prior art the design departs from: the paper describes its conditional generator and training-by-sampling as pushing resemblance so far that the model approaches a copy of the original data, leaving it exposed to membership inference, and notes that adding differential privacy to CTGAN buys that back only at the cost of utility.

The whole empirical program runs on SDV: all four baselines are SDV single-table synthesizers at default hyper-parameters, parametric Gaussian copula, CTGAN, TVAE and Copula-GAN, fidelity is the SDMetrics single-table Quality Report overall score over column shapes and column pair trends, and privacy is its discriminator AUC and DCR share.

title: Synthesizing the Counterfactual: A CTGAN-Augmented Causal Evaluation of Palliative Care on Spousal Depression

title: A Closer Look on Memorization in Tabular Diffusion Model: A Data-Centric Perspective
