title: Beyond the convexity assumption: Realistic tabular data generation under quantifier-free real linear constraints
summary: Introduces the Disjunctive Refinement Layer, which maps a generator's output into the region defined by quantifier-free linear formulas, so that background knowledge expressing non-convex or disconnected admissible spaces is satisfied by construction rather than by rejection sampling; constraint satisfaction becomes guaranteed and downstream efficacy improves. The layer is attached to five deep generative models, CTGAN and TVAE among them, giving CTGAN+DRL and TVAE+DRL, which are compared against the unmodified models and against the earlier linear-inequality layer from the same group.
evidence: the experimental section states that five DGMs are considered, WGAN, TableGAN, CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019), TVAE (Xu et al., 2019) and GOGGLE, and that DRL is built on top of each to create DGM+DRL models; the results tables report CTGAN, CTGAN+RS, CTGAN+LL and CTGAN+DRL and the matching TVAE rows across five datasets, and Figure 4 plots real, TVAE, TVAE+LL and TVAE+DRL samples in the constrained region; the introduction adopts machine learning efficacy (Xu et al., 2019) as the performance measure. Importance 4 rather than 5 follows the constrained-DGM precedent: CTGAN is one of five interchangeable substrates for a model-agnostic layer, not the thing being extended, and the paper is the successor to Stoian et al. (2024) already in the index

title: CENTS: Generating synthetic electricity consumption time series for rare and unseen scenarios
summary: Generates high-fidelity synthetic household electricity consumption traces, including rare and unobserved scenarios, for power-grid planning and simulation.

title: Cardiac mortality prediction in patients undergoing PCI based on real and synthetic data
summary: Compares five synthetic oversamplers on a registry of patients after percutaneous coronary intervention, measuring not only discrimination but calibration and confidence for each of six downstream classifiers, and finds that oversampling changes model behaviour rather than merely improving scores: recall rises at the cost of accuracy and calibration, and several generators are actively harmful. Three of the five oversamplers are SDV synthesizers, CTGAN, TVAE and GaussianCopula, each trained on the minority class and reported as its own block of results.
evidence: the synthetic data generation section describes TVAE [15] as assuming a Gaussian latent structure and Gaussian mixtures for continuous variables, CTGAN [15] as an adversarial framework for tabular data effective on imbalanced categorical features, and GaussianCopula as a copula method capturing linear dependence, reference [15] being Xu et al. (2019); the results and calibration tables carry separate blocks for models with TVAE, GAN and Gaussian Copula oversampling alongside ARF and TabSyn, and the discussion concludes that ARF and GAN oversampling are the most effective while TVAE and Gaussian Copula are less effective and often detrimental. The paper names no library for the generators, but the model names match the SDV synthesizer classes

title: Debt Collection Negotiations with Large Language Models: An Evaluation System and Optimizing Decision Making with Multi-Agent
summary: Builds an evaluation system for debt collection negotiation that scores an agent on both the negotiation process and its outcome, and proposes a multi-agent framework with planning and judging modules tuned by direct preference optimization with reject sampling. CTGAN produces the benchmark itself: the 975-record debt dataset is synthesized from real records held by a financial technology company in order to meet privacy compliance, then sampled to match the original distribution by gender, overdue days and loan amount, so every result in the paper is measured on CTGAN output.
affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Ant Group
Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Ant Group
evidence: The introduction states that to ensure both privacy and data validity CTGAN, cited to Xu et al. 2019, was used to generate synthetic data based on debt records from a leading financial technology company, and that a dataset of 975 debt records was constructed; section 2.1 repeats that CTGAN was used to generate synthetic data for privacy compliance and that the data was categorized by gender, overdue days and loan amount then sampled to match the distribution patterns of the original data; the conclusion states that by leveraging synthetic debt data generated through CTGAN the paper evaluated various AI-driven strategies

title: Diffusion and Flow Matching Models for Tabular Data: A Survey
summary: Surveys diffusion and flow-matching models for tabular data across seven task families - single-table synthesis, multi-relational synthesis, missing-value imputation, trustworthy and privacy-preserving generation, and anomaly detection - setting out a problem definition per family, a taxonomy of design choices over encoding, data-space versus latent-space generation and dependency handling, and comparative analyses of what each group of methods actually isolates. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE prior art the survey departs from: they are named as the earlier methods shown to achieve superior performance before diffusion, their Gaussian-mixture treatment of continuous features and one-hot handling of categoricals are the specific limitations the diffusion case is argued against, and the survey's own statement of the tabular modelling problem takes its notion of a complicated feature distribution from the CTGAN paper.
evidence: section II-A states that VAE-based methods such as TVAE [58] and GOGGLE were shown to achieve superior performance, then that GAN-based methods such as CTGAN [58] have shown promising results for tabular data synthesis but typically use Gaussian mixture models for continuous features, which may be suboptimal for certain real-world data, and handle categorical features with one-hot encoding, substantially increasing dimensionality; section II-B takes the phrase 'complicated distribution' for a tabular feature from [58] in setting out the survey's own problem statement; reference [58] is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni, Modeling tabular data using conditional GAN. Nothing is run - the artifact is a survey. Importance 2 under the convention for prior art a paper departs from. Curation note: this paper was curated in shards 78 and 85 as a duplicate pair and both copies were subsequently removed from main, leaving it in no shard; it is re-curated here. Two prior independent curations both reached citation_only importance 2, which this entry matches.

title: Evaluating Inter-Column Logical Relationships in Synthetic Tabular Data Generation
summary: Argues that the usual fidelity and utility measures miss whether a synthetic table preserves the logical relations that hold between its columns, and proposes three metrics for them - hierarchical consistency across nested geographic or organizational fields, mathematical and temporal dependency, and a distribution similarity index - then applies them to five generators on a real supply-chain dataset, finding that the latent-space models score well on distributional measures while failing the logical ones. CTGAN is one of the five evaluated generators, standing for the GAN category alongside SMOTE, TabDDPM, TabSyn and GReaT, and is reported across all the density, coverage, precision-recall and logical-consistency columns.
affiliations: University of Cambridge; Alan Turing Institute
evidence: the introduction credits Xu et al. 2019 with proposing a GAN variant that learns the joint distribution through a minimax game, rendered by pypdf as GTGANs, and argues it fails to capture explicit conditional dependencies; section 3 names the five representative methods selected for the experiments as SMOTE, CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019), TabDDPM, TabSyn and GReaT, each generating about 140,000 samples from the DataCo supply-chain dataset over ten repeated runs; Table 1 reports CTGAN's density estimation, correlation, coverage, alpha-precision, beta-recall and hierarchical consistency scores, and the discussion groups CTGAN with TabDDPM and TabSyn as latent-space models that are reliable distributionally but struggle with inter-column logic. Importance 3: a compared generator among five, with none of CTGAN's machinery adopted.

title: Evaluation of Generative AI Models for Processing Single-Cell RNA-Sequencing Data in Human Pancreatic Tissue
summary: Evaluates generative models on single-cell RNA sequencing, where rare cell types are exactly the ones an analysis wants to characterise and exactly the ones with fewest observations. Gaussian Copula is among the generators producing synthetic cells for the underrepresented types, an application of SDV to genomics rather than tabular records.
evidence: abstract: Gaussian Copula among generators of synthetic cells for underrepresented types

title: Exponential Family Variational Flow Matching for Tabular Data Generation
summary: Extends variational flow matching to mixed-type tables by writing the per-feature posterior as a general exponential family distribution, which turns the training objective into moment matching and so covers continuous and discrete columns in one principled form, and relates the resulting objective to generalized flow matching under Bregman divergences before evaluating the model on the standard tabular benchmark suite. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE baselines in that suite, reported on shape and trend error rates, alpha-precision, beta-recall and machine-learning efficiency across six datasets.
evidence: the baselines paragraph names the GAN-based comparator citing Xu et al. 2019, rendered in the PDF as CTAGAN, alongside VAE-based, diffusion and flow alternatives; Tables 1 and 2 report Shape and Trend error rates for CTGAN and TVAE against GOGGLE, TabDDPM, TabSyn, TabDiff and TabbyFlow on Adult, Default, Shoppers, Magic, Beijing and News; Table 3 and Table 4 rank CTGAN and TVAE on alpha-precision and beta-recall, and Table 8 reports their machine-learning efficiency AUC and RMSE against real data. Importance 3: compared generators only, with no reuse of the conditional vector or mode-specific normalization.

title: Flexible Counterfactual Explanations with Generative Models
summary: Introduces counterfactual templates that let a user name which features may change at inference time rather than fixing the mutable set when the explainer is trained, and implements them in a generative adversarial explainer that also works black-box by learning from a historical prediction dataset instead of the classifier's internals, improving counterfactual validity over optimization-based benchmarks on economic and healthcare tables. CTGAN is the foundation the model is built on: its generator and discriminator architectures serve as FCEGAN's, its training-by-sampling supplies the real counterfactuals used in the discriminator loss, and an independently trained CTGAN discriminator is the paper's fakeness metric.
affiliations: Vrije Universiteit Brussel; University of Antwerp
evidence: appendix A states that the generator and discriminator of the Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) serve as the foundation for FCEGAN, including the independent CTGAN discriminator used for assessing fakeness, with residual layers in the generator and a PacGAN discriminator; the introduction states that FCEGAN incorporates techniques from CTGAN including training-by-sampling together with WGAN-GP to mitigate mode collapse; the loss section states that the real counterfactuals compared against by the discriminator loss are selected using the training-by-sampling method described in CTGAN; Table 1 defines the fakeness quality measure as D_CTGAN applied to the counterfactual. The compared benchmarks are counterfactual-search methods, not generators, so CTGAN is the substrate throughout rather than a baseline.

title: Handling Uncertainty in Health Data using Generative Algorithms
summary: Proposes RIGA, which converts small imbalanced clinical tables into image representations so that image generative models can augment them, then converts back for tabular classifiers, tested on a preterm-birth cohort and a myocardial infarction dataset where the minority class is very small. CTGAN is the tabular augmentation baseline the image route is measured against, reported as reducing AUC on some datasets and giving a modest 0.87 per cent improvement on another, and named as the tabular GAN the authors' approach outperforms.
evidence: the related-work section states that GANs have been used to augment tabular data but their popularity is limited by challenges with mixed numerical and categorical features, that Conditional Tabular GAN (Xu et al. 2019) adapts to tabular data by normalizing mixed features and has been found to outperform other GAN-based methods, and that the authors' approach outperforms CTGAN, suggesting converting tabular data to images is productive; the nuMoM2b results state that ADASYN and SMOTE decreased XGBoost AUC while CTGAN provided minimal improvement; the myocardial results state ADASYN, SMOTE and CTGAN reduced AUC scores; a further dataset reports that CTGAN, by leveraging adversarial training, provided a modest improvement of 0.87 per cent, showing its ability to capture more meaningful feature distributions; Table 1 carries an XGBoost and CTGAN row across the datasets

title: How Well Does Your Tabular Generator Learn the Structure of Tabular Data?
summary: Argues that tabular generative models are judged by criteria imported from image and text modalities and proposes structural fidelity - the alignment of causal structure between real and synthetic tables - as a fourth evaluation dimension alongside density estimation, downstream utility and privacy, then benchmarks nine generators from eight method families over seven datasets and reports that no single generator is strong on all four. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE entries in that panel, and the benchmark's downstream-utility dimension is the train-on-synthetic test-on-real protocol adopted from Xu et al., which the paper also names as one of the inherited criteria it argues is insufficient on its own.
evidence: the introduction lists the evaluation dimensions mainstream benchmarks adopt from homogeneous modalities as density estimation, downstream utility citing Xu et al. 2019, and privacy preservation, and argues they fail to assess structural information; section 2.4 states that for all downstream tasks the authors adopt the train-on-synthetic test-on-real strategy citing Xu et al. 2019; section 2.6 lists the nine benchmark generators across eight categories, with TVAE (Xu et al. 2019) among the two VAE-based methods and CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) as the GAN method; the results tables report CTGAN and TVAE on density, alpha-precision, beta-recall, accuracy, RMSE, DCR, authenticity and local and global independence for both classification and regression datasets, and the per-generator radar figures include panels for each. Importance 3: two of nine benchmarked generators plus an adopted evaluation protocol, with no reuse of the conditional vector or mode-specific normalization.

title: Improving Cardiac Risk Prediction Using Data Generation Techniques
summary: Models cardiac rehabilitation as a business process and addresses the small, imbalanced patient records it yields by proposing conditional variational autoencoder variants with supervised and contrastive latent structure, then measuring whether classifiers trained on the augmented sets predict risk better than those trained on the original data. CTGAN is one of three publicly available generators run as the state-of-the-art comparison, with hyper-parameters from its original publication, and the paper reports it failing on this dataset: it achieves low accuracy for the at-risk class and shifts the original distribution despite being conditional.
evidence: The experimental section states the proposed architectures are compared with three state-of-the-art generative models with publicly available implementations, CTGAN, TTVAE and WGAN-GP, with hyper-parameters following the settings of the original publications; the discussion states that CTGAN, TTVAE and WGAN-GP perform noticeably below the VAE-based variants and never rank among the best-performing sets, and that CTGAN, although conditional, achieves low accuracy for the at-risk class and alters the original distribution; Table 2 reports CTGAN at doubled and quintupled synthetic set sizes against the proposed CVAE variants. Reference [21] resolves to Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni. TTVAE here is the transformer-based model of Wang and Nguyen, not SDV's TVAE

title: Large Language Models for Imbalanced Classification: Diversity makes the difference
summary: Oversamples the minority class by prompting a fine-tuned language model and then interpolating between generated and majority records, arguing that the diversity of the added samples matters more than their proximity to the real minority, and reports the best or second-best classifier accuracy on eight of ten datasets. CTGAN and TVAE are the two generative baselines among eight oversamplers, run from the sdv-dev implementation, with CTGAN the strongest competitor throughout the comparison.
affiliations: Black Dog Institute; University of New South Wales
Black Dog Institute; University of New South Wales
evidence: section 4 lists eight oversampling baselines in three groups and places CTGAN [30] and TVAE [30] as the generative-based methods between the classical SMOTE family and the LLM-based methods, footnote 3 giving github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN as the source code used; the results describe CTGAN as the runner-up and later the best baseline, report the proposed method's close-probability and coverage scores against CTGAN's, and Figure 5 sweeps the interpolation ratio against CTGAN as the reference line

title: Limited Reference, Reliable Generation: A Two-Component Framework for Tabular Data Generation in Low-Data Regimes
summary: Targets tabular generation when only tens of reference rows exist, pairing a component that distils decision-tree logic into compact rules to guide a language model with a dual-granularity filter that screens generated rows at both the instance and the chunk level, and reports gains over both deep generative and prompt-based baselines at sample sizes from 30 to 500. CTGAN reaches the paper twice: it is named in related work as the classical method the paper departs from, faulted for mode collapse and heavy preprocessing, and it is the generator underneath the DRL constraint baseline, which the hyper-parameter table labels CTGAN-based and trains for 150 epochs at batch size 24.
evidence: Section 2.1 states CTGAN, cited to Xu et al. 2019, extends GANs to handle mixed-type variables but suffers from mode collapse and requires heavy preprocessing; the experimental setup lists DRL, the Disjunctive Refinement Layers generator of Stoian and Giunchiglia 2025, as the constraint-based baseline and notes it builds on a GAN-based formulation; Table 5 gives the hyper-parameters for the non-LLM baselines and labels the row DRL (CTGAN-based) with 150 epochs, batch size 24 and Adam at 2e-4; DRL columns appear in every results table. The downloaded PDF carries the later title Rule-Guided Tabular Data Generation with Dual-Granularity Filtering; the title recorded here is the one the DOI record and citation pool carry
needs: Convention question, related to the open question on paper-constrained-dgm-realistic-2024. The rule that benchmarking a CTGAN descendant is citation_only was written for standalone descendant models such as CTAB-GAN+. Here the baseline is a constraint layer wrapped around CTGAN itself, trained with CTGAN's own hyper-parameters, so CTGAN is the generator actually run. Recorded baseline_only 3 on that reading; citation_only 2 is the alternative

title: Pre-Tactical Flight-Delay and Turnaround Forecasting with Synthetic Aviation Data
summary: Asks whether synthetic flight records can stand in for proprietary operational data in pre-tactical delay and turnaround forecasting, training four generators on 1.74 million European flights and then comparing train-on-real against train-on-synthetic across five regression algorithms and three prediction tasks, and finds 94 to 97 percent of real-data predictive performance is retained. Two of the four generators are SDV code: CTGAN, whose mode-specific normalization the paper singles out for the multimodal delay distributions, and a Gaussian copula synthesizer, both carried in the companion library as adapted copies of sdv-dev sources over a declared RDT dependency.
affiliations: SINTEF; Norwegian University of Science and Technology
evidence: phase 2 of the experimental framework trains four generative models on the real training data, Gaussian Copula, CTGAN [8], TabSyn and REaLTabFormer, reference [8] being Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni; the model description credits CTGAN's mode-specific normalization for handling delays that cluster around zero with a long tail, and Table II reports KS Complement, Chi-Squared, correlation and likelihood fidelity scores for all four. The companion repository named in footnote 1, github.com/SynthAIr/syntabair, carries src/syntabair/generators/ctgan and .../copula, whose header records the code as adapted from github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN under the Business Source License, and declares rdt as a dependency in pyproject.toml
needs: the companion library SynthAIr/syntabair is itself an index candidate as a vendored_source repository and is not yet in the pool; the paper's Gaussian copula and fidelity metric names read as SDV and SDMetrics but the paper text credits neither, so the sdv-dev attribution here rests on the repository rather than on the paper

title: Probabilistic causal graphs as categorical data synthesizers: Do they do better than Gaussian Copulas and Conditional Tabular GANs?
summary: Asks whether probabilistic causal graphs synthesise categorical data better than the general-purpose tools, on a survey of accessibility barriers, then puts the chosen synthetic set to work in an application example. Three libraries are run side by side: SDV with its Gaussian Copula synthesizer and CTGAN, DataSynthesizer with its independent and correlated attribute modes, and pyAgrum for the Bayesian network. SDV is executed as one of three co-equal arms and gets its own methods subsection.
evidence: full text, section 4.2.1 "Synthetic Data Vault (SDV)": "The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library with functions such as Gaussian Copula Synthesize, and CTGAN"; "SDV [22] is a Python library designed [for]"

title: Reinforcement-Guided Hyper-Heuristic Hyperparameter Optimization for Fair and Explainable Spiking Neural Network-Based Financial Fraud Detection
summary: Combines a cortical spiking network with population coding and a reinforcement-guided hyper-heuristic search over its hyperparameters for detecting fraudulent bank account applications, targeting accuracy alongside group fairness and explainability, and evaluates it on the six bias variants of the Bank Account Fraud suite against gradient-boosted and prior spiking baselines under a reward that trades predictive equality against parameter count. CTGAN is the generator that produced the benchmark this work runs on: the paper records that the Bank Account Fraud suite was synthesized with it to preserve applicant anonymity, and states explicitly that CTGAN belongs to the dataset's creation and not to its own training pipeline.
affiliations: Khulna University of Engineering and Technology
evidence: section 4.1.1 states that the BAF Dataset Suite is a fairness-oriented benchmark of six variations drawn from real-world online bank account applications and that synthetic data was generated using a generative adversarial network to preserve client anonymity; the software paragraph in section 4 lists CTGAN, cited to Xu et al. 2019, among the libraries employed, as used in the original dataset generation; the Rationale for No Augmentation note states that the only data augmentation in the pipeline refers to CTGAN being used to generate the BAF dataset itself, not the authors' training process, and that synthetic oversampling such as SMOTE was deliberately avoided to preserve the 1.1% fraud rate. The tight scan returns two hits in the whole PDF, both accounted for here; there is no results row for CTGAN because it was never run by these authors.
needs: no convention covers this shape. The paper never runs CTGAN, yet every row it trains and evaluates on is CTGAN output, produced by the third-party Bank Account Fraud dataset authors. Recorded citation_only importance 2 as the conservative reading of the existing scale (CTGAN described, not run). The alternative is `inherited`, whose definition - SDV arrived inside a vendored third party rather than by a decision to embed it, and the intermediary is usually an index entry in its own right - fits closely if it is read to cover a third-party dataset as well as a vendored library, with the BAF suite as the intermediary entry. Importance would then plausibly be 3 rather than 2, since the paper's entire empirical substrate is CTGAN output. Needs a ruling before other dataset-inheritance cases are judged.

title: StructSynth: Leveraging LLMs for Structure-Aware Tabular Data Synthesis in Low-Data Regimes
summary: Splits tabular synthesis into structure discovery and structure-guided generation: a directed acyclic graph is learned from the scarce real data, then supplied to a language model as an explicit blueprint of feature dependencies, so the generated rows respect the discovered structure rather than whatever correlations the model happens to infer, which improves fidelity and downstream utility over both implicit generators and unguided language models when data is thin. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the four deep generative baselines run across six datasets, and the paper's own citation trail attributes both the VAE line and the wider synthesis literature back to the Synthetic Data Vault paper.
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
evidence: the Baselines paragraph in section 4 lists TVAE (Xu et al. 2019), CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019), TabDDPM and NFlow as the deep generative model group among nine baselines; Table 2 reports CTGAN and TVAE downstream scores across Adult, Anxiety, Compas, Salary, Obesity and Churn with average ranks, and the privacy table reports their distinguishability scores on the same six; the discussion observes that CTGAN ranks highly on pairwise correlations but shows mediocre privacy and poor downstream utility; note that both the introduction and section 2 attribute VAEs and TVAE to Patki, Wedge and Veeramachaneni (2016), the Synthetic Data Vault paper, rather than to Xu et al., so the SDV paper carries part of the citation weight here

title: TabGen-ICL: Residual-Aware In-Context Example Selection for Tabular Data Generation
summary: Generates tabular data by prompting a fixed large language model rather than fine-tuning one, selecting in-context examples that cover the residual between the real distribution and what has been generated so far, so each round of prompting corrects the gap the previous round left. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN-based and VAE-based entries among the deep generative baselines it is measured against on marginal, correlation, precision, recall, C2ST and Jensen-Shannon divergence.
evidence: Section 2 describes CTGAN and TVAE, both cited to Xu et al. 2019, as dealing with mixed-type tabular data generation under the GAN and VAE frameworks; section 5 lists the deep generative baselines as the VAE-based method TVAE, the GAN-based method CTGAN, four diffusion methods and two autoregressive methods, alongside LLM-based methods with and without fine-tuning; the results table reports TVAE and CTGAN rows on marginal, correlation, precision, recall, C2ST and JSD against TABGEN-ICL

title: TabTreeFormer: Tabular Data Generation Using Hybrid Tree-Transformer
summary: Argues that transformers applied to tables lack the inductive biases that make tree ensembles effective on them, and answers with a hybrid in which a tree model supplies leaf-index prompts to the transformer while a dual-quantization tokenizer, K-means for modes and quantiles for precision, shortens sequences and shrinks the vocabulary, reaching competitive utility at a fraction of the model size. CTGAN is the acknowledged source of the multimodal-decomposition idea the tokenizer replaces and of the conditional generation the paper extends from single columns to clusters, but it is not among the eight generators run, where CTAB-GAN+ stands in for the GAN family.
evidence: section 1 states that the dual-quantization tokenization is inspired by Xu et al. (2019), which addresses multimodal continuous features via multimodal decomposition; section 2.1 records that CTGAN uses a variational Gaussian mixture model to decompose multimodal values; section 3 notes that many early tabular frameworks use conditional generation (Xu et al. 2019) based on the values of a specific column and that TabTreeFormer extends the condition to clusters with multiple concurrent conditions; the baselines in section 4 are Forest Diffusion, CTAB-GAN+, TTVAE, TabSyn, GReaT, REaLTabFormer, TabMT and TabuLa, with no CTGAN or TVAE row in the utility, fidelity, privacy or efficiency tables. SDMetrics re-read (correction shard 91). The arXiv lane's scan patterns are CTGAN-centric: 'SDMetrics' and 'SDGym' appear in neither the loose nor the tight pattern, and 'sdv.dev' is in the loose one only, where a high CTGAN hit-count buries it. A sweep of all 84 lane PDFs for SDV tool names found this entry named a tool its facets did not record. Appendix D.5 (Fidelity Metrics Implementation) states that fidelity metrics are calculated using SDMetrics' public SDK. CTGAN itself remains cited rather than benchmarked - the eight baselines are Forest Diffusion, CTAB-GAN+, TTVAE, TabSyn, GReaT and others - so the prior citation_only reading of CTGAN was right, but an SDV tool is executed. Integration moves to api_user on the DP-CGANS precedent that executing an SDV-family tool outranks a comparison or citation role; importance reflects how much of the evaluation that tool carries. Importance 3: SDMetrics carries the fidelity third of a utility/fidelity/privacy evaluation. Prior values: citation_only importance 2.

title: Tabby: A Language Model Architecture for Tabular and Structured Data Synthesis
summary: Modifies a standard transformer language model for tabular synthesis by replacing selected layers with Gated Mixture-of-Experts blocks that give each column its own parameters, pairs this with a simpler row-serialisation training scheme, and reports quality at or near that of real data across eight tables and one nested JSON dataset. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE representatives among the non-language-model baselines, carried as rows through the machine-learning-efficacy, discrimination and distance-to-closest-record tables.
evidence: the Non-LLM Approaches paragraph in section 4 names CTGAN and TVAE, both cited to Xu et al. (2019), as the leading GAN and VAE approaches included alongside CTAB-GAN+ and four diffusion models; Table 2 reports CTGAN and TVAE machine-learning-efficacy scores across Diabetes, Travel, Adult, Magic, Shoppers, Abalone, Rainfall and House, and later tables report their discrimination and distance-to-closest-record scores on the same tables; section 5 notes that CTGAN and TVAE, unlike Tabby, do not clearly extend beyond tabular data to nested structures. SDMetrics re-read (correction shard 91). The arXiv lane's scan patterns are CTGAN-centric: 'SDMetrics' and 'SDGym' appear in neither the loose nor the tight pattern, and 'sdv.dev' is in the loose one only, where a high CTGAN hit-count buries it. A sweep of all 84 lane PDFs for SDV tool names found this entry named a tool its facets did not record. The metrics section states that Shape (Table 8) follows the SDMetrics library's implementation, using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and the complement of total variation distance averaged across columns, and that Trend (Table 9) again uses the SDMetrics library's implementation, measuring Pearson correlation between numerical columns and the complement of total variation distance for categorical pairs. Integration moves to api_user on the DP-CGANS precedent that executing an SDV-family tool outranks a comparison or citation role; importance reflects how much of the evaluation that tool carries. Importance 3: two of the paper's reported metric tables. Prior values: baseline_only importance 3.

title: Task Decoding based on Eye Movements using Synthetic Data Augmentation
summary: Revisits Yarbus's claim that the viewing task can be read off the eye movements, on a dataset small enough that the spatial-temporal classifiers it wants to use cannot be trained directly. Synthetic participants fill the gap, generated by three systems and compared. Two of the three are SDV's — CTGAN and CopulaGAN, the latter existing nowhere outside the library — with Gretel's hosted CTGAN as the third, so SDV is run to produce the augmentation the classification results depend on.
evidence: full text: "we have used CTGAN [12], CopulaGAN [12], and Gretel [11] API-based CTGAN algorithms to generate synthetic data"; "we used the widely popular CTGAN architecture and its variants CopulaGAN in this paper"

title: Toward Valid Generative Clinical Trial Data with Survival Endpoints
summary: Generates synthetic control arms for late-phase oncology and rare-disease trials by learning covariates and the time-to-event endpoint jointly in one latent variational model rather than in the two-stage pipeline the GAN-based survival generators use, so that censoring and small sample sizes are handled inside the generative model instead of by a separate downstream time regressor. TVAE runs inside the comparison: the Surv-VAE arm is the SurvivalGAN pipeline with its GAN covariate module replaced by the tabular variational autoencoder of Xu et al., while CTGAN and TVAE as standalone generators were considered and excluded on the strength of SurvivalGAN's earlier finding that they are less effective for survival modelling.
affiliations: Organisation Mondiale de la Santé Animale
Organisation Mondiale de la Santé Animale
Organisation Mondiale de la Santé Animale
Hôpital Européen Georges-Pompidou; Centre d'Investigation Clinique Hôpital Européen Georges Pompidou
Organisation Mondiale de la Santé Animale
evidence: the related-work section names TGAN, TVAE (Xu et al. 2019) and CTAB-GAN among the data-driven generative models applied to tabular clinical datasets; section 3.2 states that other tabular data generators such as CTGAN, TVAE or normalizing flows were compared to SurvivalGAN in Norcliffe et al. 2023 and found less effective for survival modelling, and were therefore excluded from this paper's comparison, leaving Surv-GAN and Surv-VAE as the two competing methods; appendix A.1 states that SurvivalVAE adopts the same pipeline framework as SurvivalGAN, replacing the GAN module with a Tabular Variational Autoencoder (Xu et al. 2019) to generate covariates. Importance 3: TVAE is executed as the covariate generator inside one of the two compared methods rather than benchmarked directly, and none of CTGAN's conditional vector or mode-specific normalization is adopted.

title: What's Wrong with Your Synthetic Tabular Data? Using Explainable AI to Evaluate Generative Models
summary: Turns synthetic-data evaluation into an explanation problem: a discriminator is trained to tell real records from synthetic ones, and feature importance, feature effect and counterfactual methods are then applied to that discriminator to say which columns, value ranges and interactions the generator got wrong, rather than returning a single quality score. CTGAN is one of six synthesizers whose detectability is compared, and the appendix works the full diagnosis through on ten CTGAN-generated nursery datasets.
affiliations: Leibniz Institute for Prevention Research and Epidemiology (BIPS); University of Bremen

title: Debiasing Synthetic Data Generated by Deep Generative Models

title: Unmasking Trees for Tabular Data
summary: Presents UnmaskingTrees, which fits gradient-boosted decision trees to incrementally unmask individual features for tabular imputation and generation, together with BaltoBot, a balanced-tree conditional density estimator that turns any probabilistic binary classifier into a generative model, and reports leading imputation performance on a 27-dataset out-of-the-box benchmark. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the compared generators: the paper repeats the experimental setup of Jolicoeur-Martineau et al. and reports their average ranks across nine metrics both on complete data and under 20 percent missingness.
evidence: Section 3.2 states the paper repeats the experimental setup of Jolicoeur-Martineau et al. 2024b on the same 27 datasets, whose benchmark compares Gaussian Copula, tabular variational autoencoding (TVAE) and the conditional GAN methods CTGAN and CTAB-GAN+ against two diffusion methods under nine metrics in the fully observed and 20 percent MCAR settings; the two ranking tables report TVAE and CTGAN rows alongside UnmaskingTrees on Wtrain, Wtest, coverage, R2fake, F1fake, F1disc, Pbias and covrate. A GaussianCopula row appears in the same tables but the paper attributes it to Joe 2014 rather than to SDV, so only CTGAN and TVAE are recorded here. SDMetrics re-read (correction shard 91). The arXiv lane's scan patterns are CTGAN-centric: 'SDMetrics' and 'SDGym' appear in neither the loose nor the tight pattern, and 'sdv.dev' is in the loose one only, where a high CTGAN hit-count buries it. A sweep of all 84 lane PDFs for SDV tool names found this entry named a tool its facets did not record. The results tables rank GaussianCopula alongside TVAE, CTGAN and CTAB-GAN+ across Wasserstein, coverage, downstream and discriminator columns on 27 datasets, so an SDV-family copula generator is run as a compared baseline. Facet correction only: integration baseline_only and importance 3 were already correct.

title: A Range-based Association Rule and GAN-based Hybrid Approach for Imbalanced Classification
summary: Combines range-based association rule sampling with a modified tabular GAN to handle imbalanced classification in automation settings. The modification to the generator makes this a derivative rather than a use, though the abstract does not state which parts were changed.
evidence: abstract: combines association-rule sampling with a modified tabular GAN

title: Balanced Marginal and Joint Distributional Learning via Mixture Cramer-Wold Distance
summary: Notes that a generative model trained on a joint distributional distance can score well on joint metrics while fitting individual columns poorly, and proposes a mixture Cramer-Wold distance that adds marginal reconstruction to the joint objective, so a denoising autoencoder learns both at once with a tunable trade-off. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five synthesizers it is measured against on marginal and joint similarity, distance to closest record and attribute disclosure, all trained at the same latent dimension with their hyperparameters recorded.
evidence: the experimental section states the model is compared with the state-of-the-art synthesizers CTGAN, TVAE, CTAB-GAN, CW2 and DistVAE, all at latent dimension two; Table 3 records the epochs, batch size and learning rate for CTGAN and TVAE; Table 6 ranks them on Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Wasserstein, pairwise correlation difference, log-cluster and F1, and Table 7 on distance to closest record and attribute disclosure

title: C3-TGAN: Controllable Tabular Data Synthesis with Explicit Correlations and Property Constraints
summary: Argues that GAN-based tabular synthesis ignores explicit attribute correlations and property constraints, so downstream analysis of the synthetic data can reach wrong conclusions even when marginals look right. C3-TGAN adds both to the tabular GAN, a named derivative that extends the architecture rather than applying it.
affiliations: Harbin Institute of Technology; Peng Cheng Laboratory
Harbin Institute of Technology; Peng Cheng Laboratory
evidence: abstract: C3-TGAN adds explicit correlation and property constraints to tabular GAN synthesis

title: Curated LLM: Synergy of LLMs and Data Curation for tabular augmentation in low-data regimes
summary: Argues that in the low-data regime a generator fitted to a handful of rows cannot invent structure it never saw, and proposes drawing candidate rows from a large language model's prior instead, then discarding the ones a learning-dynamics curation step marks as hard or ambiguous, so only samples the downstream model can actually use survive. CTGAN and TVAE are the conventional tabular generators the argument is set against and the comparison is run against: TVAE is the head-to-head generator in the extrapolation study and in the per-subgroup accuracy gains, where it loses ground on the smallest groups while the language model gains.
evidence: section 2.1 states that in the low-data regime conventional tabular generative models such as CTGAN and TVAE are constrained by the limited training set and may not generate sufficiently diverse or accurate synthetic data, which is the motivation for the language-model approach; the extrapolation study compares samples generated by GPT-4 against TVAE described as a widely used tabular data generator; the subgroup table reports average accuracy gains for GPT-4 against TVAE across the smallest subgroups

title: Deep Generative Models, Synthetic Tabular Data, and Differential Privacy: An Overview and Synthesis
summary: Synthesises the literature on deep generative models for tabular data under differential privacy, setting variational autoencoders, normalizing flows, GANs and diffusion models in a common probabilistic notation and then tracing how each has been fitted with privacy guarantees, with attention to where the tabular setting breaks assumptions carried over from images. CTGAN is presented as the reference set of refinements for the tabular GAN, named for mode-specific normalization and conditioning vectors and for carrying both across to the VAE in the same work; later methods are described by what they replace in it, such as an inverse-CDF transform standing in for its mode-specific normalization. Nothing is run.
evidence: the section on GANs for tabular data states that several refinements of a basic GAN approach are considered in the conditional tabular GAN approach of Xu et al. 2019, namely mode-specific normalization and conditioning vectors, and that the same work applies these to VAE models; a following paragraph describes Li et al.'s inverse-CDF GAN as replacing the mode-specific normalization in CTGAN with a transformation based on an estimated cumulative distribution function

title: Differentially Private Diffusion Models Generate Useful Synthetic Images
summary: Shows that diffusion models can be trained under differential privacy to a standard where classifiers trained purely on their output are competitive on image benchmarks, using public pre-training, large batches and augmentation multiplicity to make private training tractable. The SDV paper and DP-CTGAN appear only in the bibliography, and CTGAN is cited once inside a list of differentially private GAN work; the paper is an image-domain study and runs nothing from the SDV family.
evidence: the related-work paragraph on differentially private generative models cites Xu et al. 2019 within an undifferentiated list of GAN references; the bibliography carries both the Patki et al. Synthetic Data Vault paper and Fang et al. DP-CTGAN; no SDV-family model is trained or evaluated anywhere in the paper, whose experiments are on image datasets

title: Distributed Conditional GAN (discGAN) For Synthetic Healthcare Data Generation
summary: Proposes discGAN, a distributed conditional GAN for synthetic electronic health records, in which discriminators sit with the data at each site so that patient records never leave their holder, evaluated on ICU stay records by machine-learning efficacy, Kolmogorov-Smirnov and chi-squared tests. CTGAN is the state of the art the design is written against: the literature survey gives it its own section headed as the conditional tabular model from the Synthetic Data Vault, the paper takes its account of the discrete-and-continuous modelling problem from it, and discGAN's architecture is defined by contrast, dropping the residual block the CTGAN implementation uses. CTGAN itself is not run.
evidence: the literature survey section II.A is headed CTGAN: Modeling Conditional Tabular Data from Synthetic Data Vault and describes it as the state-of-the-art tabular generator from MIT; the model section states the paper uses methods described in the CTGAN reference to produce single-table synthetic data and quotes its account of simultaneously modelling discrete and continuous columns; the architecture subsection states discGAN forewent adding residual blocks, opposed to the SOTA CTGAN implementation; no experiment trains or samples CTGAN

title: Distributional Learning of Variational AutoEncoder: Application to Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Attacks the Gaussianity assumption in variational autoencoders by replacing the reconstruction term with a continuous ranked probability score, so that the decoder estimates conditional quantiles and the model learns the full distribution rather than reconstructing points, with theorems showing the objective recovers the ground-truth distribution. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the three generators DistVAE is benchmarked against across six tabular datasets, on machine-learning utility, correlation structure, marginal similarity, distance to closest record and attribute disclosure, with per-model hyperparameters and parameter counts reported.
evidence: Table 1 reports CTGAN, TVAE and CTAB-GAN against DistVAE on MARE and F1; Table 2 gives their correlation-matrix distances; later tables report their Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Wasserstein marginal similarity, distance to closest record and attribute disclosure at three neighbour counts; Table 9 lists the epochs, batch size and learning rate used for CTGAN and TVAE and Table 10 their parameter counts per dataset

title: Diverse Community Data for Benchmarking Data Privacy Algorithms
summary: Publishes a set of curated excerpts from American Community Survey data, chosen so that privacy algorithms can be tested on small, tractable populations whose subgroup structure is visible, and pairs them with an evaluation suite that surfaces defects aggregate utility scores hide. CTGAN, listed as the SDV implementation, is one of the synthesizers run across the excerpts as the non-differentially-private neural comparator, and the analysis reports it failing to preserve constraints that hold for child records and dropping a housing-feature constraint.
affiliations: National Institute of Standards and Technology
evidence: Table 1 lists SDV CTGAN among the evaluated deidentification methods, categorised as non-DP synthetic data from a generative adversarial network, with its reported utility and subsample percentages; the results discussion states that CTGAN is not preserving constraints that hold for child records and is missing a constraint on housing features, alongside a propensity and PCA comparison of the three neural synthesizers

title: Fs-TGAN: An Enhanced Approach for IoT Intrusion Detection Based on Feature Selection and Tabular GAN
summary: Proposes an IoT intrusion detection approach pairing feature selection with a tabular GAN. The name Fs-TGAN indicates a TGAN variant, but no abstract is indexed, so whether the generator is modified or merely applied is unestablished.
evidence: title names Fs-TGAN, an apparent TGAN variant; no abstract indexed
needs: fetch the full text and establish whether the generator is modified or applied unchanged

title: MargCTGAN: A "Marginally" Better CTGAN for the Low Sample Regime
summary: Observes that synthetic tabular data is usually judged only by downstream task usefulness and that this hides how models behave when the real sample is small, then evaluates several generators across fidelity, utility and marginal statistics in the low-sample regime, finding CTGAN strong on attribute fidelity but weak on utility while TableGAN is the reverse. MargCTGAN is the paper's answer to that split: it is built on CTGAN and adds feature matching of decorrelated marginals in the principal component space, keeping the rest of the model, and improves utility without giving up the fidelity CTGAN already had.
affiliations: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security
CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security
CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security
evidence: the abstract states that to capitalize on the strengths of both models the paper proposes MargCTGAN, which improves upon CTGAN by introducing feature matching of decorrelated marginals in the principal component space, and that this consistently improves utility; the same passage reports the popular CTGAN model demonstrating high attribute fidelity but falling short in utility for low-data scenarios; section 3 describes MargCTGAN as adhering to the standard GAN paradigm with generator and discriminator

title: Membership Inference Attacks against Synthetic Data through Overfitting Detection
summary: Reframes membership inference against synthetic data as overfitting detection: DOMIAS scores a target record by the ratio of its density under the synthetic distribution to its density under a reference population, so that records the generator has locally overfitted are identified without assuming the attacker knows the training procedure. TVAE, released with CTGAN, is the generator the attack is developed and calibrated against — training-set size and epoch count are swept on TVAE to control how much it overfits, the private heart-failure experiment generates from TVAE, and CTGAN and TVAE both appear in the wider comparison of generators by privacy-utility trade-off.
affiliations: University of Cambridge; Alan Turing Institute
evidence: section 5.1 states the California Housing experiments use TVAE to generate synthetic data and vary the number of TVAE training samples and training epochs; the medical experiment generates synthetic data from TVAE on a private heart-failure dataset of about 40,000 records; the generator comparison evaluates GAN, WGAN-GP, CTGAN and TVAE, NFlow, PATE-GAN, PrivBayes and ADS-GAN, reporting CTGAN on the unfavourable side of the additive-noise curve

title: MissDiff: Training Diffusion Models on Tabular Data with Missing Values
summary: Trains diffusion models directly on tables that contain missing values, masking the regression loss for unobserved entries so the score is learned without first imputing, and shows the resulting estimator is consistent under missing-at-random assumptions where impute-then-generate pipelines are not. CTGAN and TVAE appear once, inside the paper's description of a diffusion baseline reported to outperform them by a large margin; neither is run here.
affiliations: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
evidence: the baselines section describes STaSy as the state-of-the-art diffusion model on tabular data which outperforms MedGAN, VEEGAN, CTGAN, TVAE, TableGAN, OCTGAN and RNODE by a large margin, which is the only mention of either model in the body; the CTGAN paper appears in the bibliography and no experiment in the paper trains or samples it

title: Mixed-Type Tabular Data Synthesis with Score-based Diffusion in Latent Space
summary: Argues that diffusion applied directly to mixed-type tables must contend with one-hot categorical columns that do not diffuse well, and proposes TabSyn, which first learns a joint continuous latent space with a transformer variational autoencoder and then runs score-based diffusion inside it, so that a single Gaussian process covers numerical and categorical columns at once and sampling needs few steps. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE baselines among the seven methods it is measured against across six datasets.
affiliations: Amazon Web Services; George Mason University
evidence: the baselines paragraph states the first two of seven comparisons are the classical GAN and VAE models, CTGAN and TVAE, both from Xu et al. 2019; the related-work section credits Xu et al. with proposing CTGAN and TVAE to deal with imbalanced categorical features; the results tables report CTGAN and TVAE column-wise distribution scores on Adult, Default, Shoppers, Magic, Beijing and News

title: RCT-Twin-GAN Generates Digital Twins of Randomized Control Trials Adapted to Real-world Patients
summary: Simulates randomized trial effects in real-world populations by generating a digital twin of a trial whose covariate patterns match an electronic health record, addressing the historical underrepresentation of key groups in trial cohorts. The model is CTGAN modified: an adapted loss and multi-covariate conditioning are layered onto its conditional architecture, making this a named clinical derivative rather than a use.
affiliations: Yale New Haven Hospital; Yale University
evidence: abstract: improves on CTGAN with an adapted loss and multi-covariate conditioning

title: REaLTabFormer: Generating Realistic Relational and Tabular Data using Transformers
summary: Generates relational datasets with transformers rather than statistical models: a GPT-style model learns the parent table, and a sequence-to-sequence model conditioned on the frozen parent encoding produces the child rows, with an overfitting criterion based on a statistical bootstrap deciding when to stop training. SDV is the relational baseline the result is measured against — the paper identifies the Hierarchical Modeling Algorithm of Patki et al., which fits Gaussian copulas within and across tables, as the existing approach for relational synthesis, and its figures plot SDV's output beside REaLTabFormer's on the parent-child joint distributions and on a daily sales series.
evidence: the related-work section states that models able to produce relational datasets are limited, citing Patki et al., and that existing models are based on Hierarchical Modeling Algorithms in which Gaussian copulas learn the joint distributions for each and across tables; Figure 2 plots the daily mean of the Rossmann sales variable for the original data, REaLTabFormer and SDV, and Figure 3 compares the parent-child joint distributions of the original data, SDV and REaLTabFormer

title: ResBit: Residual Bit Vector for Categorical Values
summary: Replaces one-hot encoding of categorical values with residual bit vectors, a hierarchical binary representation whose length grows logarithmically rather than linearly in cardinality, so that tables with high-cardinality columns stay tractable for generative models that would otherwise blow up in input dimension. CTGAN and TVAE are the first two of six baselines, named as the de facto standards for tabular generation, and the analysis reports CTGAN winning F1 on one dataset, failing on a highly imbalanced one, and both models losing sample diversity.
evidence: the baselines paragraph states that six existing methods are used and that the first two are CTGAN and TVAE as the de facto standards, alongside TabDDPM, CoDi, StaSy and TabSyn; the introduction describes TVAE and CTGAN as the models applying VAE and GAN to tabular data generation and still used as baselines in the field; the results discussion reports CTGAN outperforming on F1 for the AR dataset, failing to generate effectively on the imbalanced CC dataset, and both CTGAN and TVAE showing a loss of diversity

title: Semantic Representation of Physical Activity Sensor Observations and Comparative Analysis of Real and Synthetic Datasets
summary: Represents physical activity sensor observations semantically and compares real against synthetic versions of the same stream, working from wearable data collected at scale. Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and TabGAN generate the synthetic datasets, so two SDV synthesizers sit alongside an outside generator in the comparison.
affiliations: University of Agder; Simula Metropolitan Center for Digital Engineering
Simula Metropolitan Center for Digital Engineering
evidence: abstract: Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and TabGAN used to generate sensor observation data

title: Subpopulation-Specific Synthetic EHR for Better Mortality Prediction
summary: Identifies the subpopulations on which a mortality-prediction model underperforms, generates synthetic records for each of them separately, and trains a per-subpopulation ensemble on the augmented data, reporting gains over both a real-data-only ensemble and SMOTE on two MIMIC use cases. CTGAN is the generator throughout: one model is trained per underrepresented subpopulation on training-set samples only and then sampled to add between 0 and 1000 percent of that subpopulation's real size.
evidence: the related-work section states that Xu et al. proposed the Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN), which is used in this research; section 3.1 step 2 trains a CTGAN on each underrepresented subpopulation until convergence on an RTX6000, with discriminator and generator learning rates, discriminator steps, epochs and batch size given in Table 1, and step 3 samples 0 to 1000 percent of the subpopulation size; Table 2 reports ROCAUC at the best augmentation level against a real-only per-subpopulation ensemble and against SMOTE, and the discussion describes the work as applying CTGAN together with an ensemble-like approach

title: SurvivalGAN: Generating Time-to-Event Data for Survival Analysis
summary: Identifies two failure modes specific to generating survival data, short-sightedness in the time axis and poor coverage of the censoring process, and proposes SurvivalGAN, which generates covariates first and then draws the time-to-event from a separate survival model conditioned on them, so that Kaplan-Meier curves of the synthetic data track the real ones. The tabular encoder it depends on is CTGAN's: a Gaussian mixture is fitted per continuous feature and the encoder built from it, following Xu et al. directly, and CTGAN and TVAE are also two of the five generators the result is measured against across four clinical datasets.
affiliations: University of Cambridge; Alan Turing Institute
evidence: section 4 states the paper follows the approach by Xu et al. 2019, training a Gaussian Mixture Model with NC components per continuous feature and defining the tabular encoder from it, giving training and generation over mixed continuous and categorical variables; the baselines are listed as ADS-GAN, CTGAN, TVAE, PrivBayes and NFlows; the results tables report CTGAN and TVAE on Wasserstein distance, short-sightedness, KM divergence, precision, recall and density, and the hyperparameter table records a CTGAN embedding width for the model's own encoder

title: SynDiffix: More accurate synthetic structured data
summary: Presents SynDiffix, an anonymising structured-data synthesizer built on the Diffix line of work, and argues that being able to run a query over synthetic data is not the same as getting an accurate answer, reporting over twice the median accuracy of the alternatives. SDV appears as one of five compared products: CTGAN 0.18.0 is taken from sdv.dev and is the named point of comparison in the abstract, so the library is run purely as the baseline the new tool is measured against.
affiliations: Max Planck Institute for Software Systems
evidence: full text: "Compared to CTGAN, as implemented by SDV [4], the median performance of SynDiffix has over two times [better accuracy]"; synthesis products table lists "CTGAN 0.18.0 business source sdv.dev/"; "CTGAN ... is from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV)"

title: Synthetic data, real errors: how (not) to publish and use synthetic data
summary: Warns that conclusions drawn on synthetic data need not transfer to the real data behind it, because a single synthetic dataset hides the generative model's own uncertainty, and proposes publishing a Deep Generative Ensemble instead: several generators fitted to the same real data, so a downstream user can measure how much a finding depends on which model produced the rows. CTGAN is the generator the whole argument is instantiated on, chosen for its widespread use and for the diversity between independently trained instances, run with fixed hyperparameters across every experiment and varied in hidden-layer count for the demonstration that train-on-synthetic conclusions diverge from real ones.
affiliations: University of Cambridge; Alan Turing Institute
evidence: the experimental setup states the paper chooses a GAN architecture, specifically CTGAN, for its widespread use and its high expected diversity between individually trained models compared with VAEs, and that CTGAN is used with the same hyperparameters and architecture in all experiments; the motivating figure generates synthetic SEER prostate cancer data with CTGAN at different numbers of hidden layers and compares train-on-synthetic against train-on-real classification results

title: Synthpop++: A Hybrid Framework for Generating A Country-scale Synthetic Population
summary: Builds Synthpop++, a country-scale synthetic population for India that layers four data sources of differing granularity, using iterative proportional updating where marginals exist and a learned generator where they do not, and validating the result against held-out survey distributions. CTGAN supplies the attributes marginals cannot reach: it is trained on Individual and Household microdata and conditioned on age and sex to attach weight, height, comorbidities and job description to each synthetic person, and the paper selects it over statistical alternatives for handling mixed types, high dimensionality and imbalanced categoricals.
evidence: the method section states that matching only marginal distributions is not enough and that CTGAN is used for adding individual-level attributes for which marginals are not available, noting the model can be conditioned on attributes already present in the base population; a later passage states that for weight, height and comorbidities a CTGAN model conditioned on age and sex is used, trained on the subset of the IHDS-II dataset for Maharashtra, with Individual and Household microdata as CTGAN input

title: TabMT: Generating tabular data with masked transformers
summary: Applies masked transformers to tabular generation, treating each cell as a token to be predicted from the unmasked remainder, with ordered embeddings for numerical fields and a dedicated category for missing values so that incomplete tables train without imputation. TVAE is one of the four generators it is measured against, selected as the strongest VAE-based tabular baseline, and the comparison covers downstream classification accuracy across a range of datasets alongside correlation-error and privacy analyses.
evidence: the prior-methods paragraph states that four techniques are selected, one from each major family, and describes TVAE as coming from one of the first deep tabular generation papers which introduced both a GAN and a VAE, with the VAE chosen as the strongest VAE tabular generator; the results table reports TVAE alongside CTabGAN+, REaLTabFormer and TabDDPM on downstream accuracy across datasets

title: TransCORALNet: A Two-Stream Transformer CORAL Networks for Supply Chain Credit Assessment Cold Start
summary: Attacks the cold-start problem in supply-chain credit assessment, where a new industry has no labelled default history, with a two-stream transformer whose shared-weight encoders take source-industry records in one stream and target-industry records in the other, aligned by a CORAL domain-adaptation loss and explained through LIME. CTGAN supplies the target stream: it is trained to model the target-domain feature distribution and the synthetic records it produces are what the lower stream consumes, so the cold-start result depends on it.
evidence: the contributions state that to facilitate the cold start problem the paper adopts a GAN-based method, CTGAN, to model tabular data distribution and generate synthetic data by learning the probability distribution of the features in the target domain; the architecture section states the lower stream's input is synthetic target training data generated by the CTGAN approach, with encoder blocks and fully connected layers sharing weights across the two streams; the framework figure includes the CTGAN procedures as a labelled component

title: Utility Theory of Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Builds a theory of when synthetic data is useful, separating the utility of a downstream model trained on synthetic rows into a term for how well the generator approximates the real distribution and a term for the downstream task itself, and shows that closing the distributional gap is sufficient without requiring the generator to be consistent everywhere. The empirical program rests entirely on SDV: CopulaGAN, GaussianCopula, CTGAN and TVAE are the four generators the theory is instantiated on, each trained at varying sample sizes and scored through a downstream linear SVM.
evidence: the simulation section states that four generative models are considered, Copula GAN attributed to Patki et al. 2016, Gaussian Copula, CTGAN from Xu et al. 2019, and TVAE, with a linear SVM as the downstream task; Figure 3 plots the utility measure under varying training sample sizes with a panel for each of Copula GAN, Gaussian Copula, VAE and CTGAN

title: A Constructive GAN-based Approach to Exact Estimate Treatment Effect without Matching
summary: Replaces the matching step in counterfactual inference with a generative one: two conditional GANs learn the joint densities of the treatment and control groups, conditional average treatment effects are read off as the difference between the two conditional densities at the same covariate value, and their ensemble average over the treated sample is the estimate of the average treatment effect on the treated, which sidesteps the sample dropping and lack of common support that matching suffers in high dimensions. CTGAN is the generator the estimator is built on, taken from its Python code as documented on sdv.dev and run with a single merged network conditioned on a treatment one-hot vector in place of two separate ones.
evidence: section 3.3 states that to make the estimator applicable to tabular economic datasets the training proceeds through CTGAN as proposed by Xu et al. (2019), crediting its conditional generator and training-by-sampling algorithm for handling mixed continuous and discrete inputs; the following paragraph says the joint densities are learned by a method equivalent to CTGAN's Python code, with footnote 2 pointing at https://sdv.dev/SDV/user_guides/single_table/ctgan.html, and that the only difference from the original method is merging two separate GANs into one trained by distinguishing a one-hot input vector, done to save computing resources; section 5 reports that CTGAN's own evaluation criteria including KL distance and KS statistic can fail at high covariate dimension, which the authors work around by re-running training with adjusted hyperparameters and layer scales

title: Adversarial random forests for density estimation and generative modeling
summary: Proposes adversarial random forests, which alternate between fitting a forest to discriminate real from synthetic data and resampling until the two are indistinguishable, yielding a density estimator (FORDE) and a generator (FORGE) that match deep tabular models on accuracy at a small fraction of their training cost. The real-data evaluation is Xu et al.'s tabular benchmark reproduced in full, with CTGAN and TVAE run from the SDV API implementations as two of the five deep baselines.
affiliations: Leibniz Institute for Prevention Research and Epidemiology (BIPS); University of Bremen
Leibniz Institute for Prevention Research and Epidemiology (BIPS); University of Bremen
Leibniz Institute for Prevention Research and Epidemiology (BIPS); University of Bremen; University of Copenhagen
